Metro Centre Mayhem Update

By: Harri Vithi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
When a civil servant takes service delivery to the next level.

Unique Selling Point:
When an insider becomes the accused.

Summary:
In June, we went inside the Metro Centre through a an extremely helpful civil servant. Little did we know, that three months later our inside man would be accused of selling the very building plans he's meant to organize.

Further information:
In June this year, Norman Munyai was every so kind to let Carte Blanche into the Metro Centre so we could grant our viewers access to the City rot. As we walked through corridors, upstairs and took elevators - Norman related what a horrible working environment the City nursed. This was evidenced by the state of the archives and the fact that Norman had to work in a supposedly condemned building for 2 hours a day.

But one could never have guessed that Norman would turn the messy archives into a side hustle - selling business plans to the residents meant to get them for free.

Daniel Schay was first to learn of Norman's dirty scheme and when we put our heads together - we realized his wayward City official had once been our civil servant hero.
We tried to set Norman up on a sting but the Sunday Times expose made him go to ground.
Now we tell the story of how a lack of service delivery creates the opportunity for corruption.

MNet Text Script: Metro Mayhem Update

(Masa) Behind every building, from high rises to suburban homes, lies a crucial document: a building plan.They’re kept in the archives at the Joburg Metro Centre.
(Sarah Wissler) I've been in them, in 2016/2017 it looked like this, exactly like this! Stuff strewn everywhere.
(Masa) Two years ago, the Metro Centre was condemned. The City relocated thousands of employees but left about one million building plans behind… in a state of chaos.
(Insider) (Subtitles) They’re supposed to put the boards ..this is Joburg, Sandton.
(Producer) (Subtitles) Jah there's no boards.
(Insider) (Subtitles) Nothing.
(Producer) (Subtitles) Guys, are you looking for files with a torch?
(Insider) (Subtitles) Yes.
(Masa) The result? People hoping to sell or renovate their homes unable to find their plans and forced to have them redrawn - at their own cost.

(Heather Dodd) This is an apartment building in Illovo, where we did extensive measuring up of an existing building that took a week and a half on site measuring up.

(Masa) In the City of Joburg, a lack of service delivery opens opportunities to back door hustles.

(Daniel Schay) It is a catch 22. Whether with building plans or when they don't have electricity or they have a water issue, they've got to either pay a bribe or not get service in Johannesburg because of the way things are run.

(Masa) In June this year, our expose into the state of the Metro Centre archives revealed how the City is struggling to keep up with even its own paperwork. It was outside these doors that we met a seemingly helpful insider who gave us access to the building.
(Insider) You see the distance that we walk to come here to search the files.
(Masa) It was a long walk to the basement archives, through corridors, parking lots and up stairs.

(Masa) Inside, plans had tumbled from shelves and piled up on every available surface.
(Masa) It’s the job of our insider to retrieve building plans from these chaotic archives for residents.
(Producer) (Subtitles) Even if you wanted to do your job…
(Insider)(Subtitles) You can’t.
(Producer) (Subtitles) How do you do your job?
(Insider) (Subtitles) But what about the public? They are losing money for nothing.
(Producer) (Subtitles) So they're losing money because they can't do the developments?
(Insider) (Subtitles) Yes. And when you come and ask for the plans and when we don’t find them, you must go to redraw with your money.
(Masa) At the time, we didn’t realise we'd stumbled on more than a service delivery issue.

(Masa) The DA’s Daniel Schay says he was approached by a concerned resident earlier this month.

(Daniel Schay) So the first resident approached me and said you won't believe what happened when I tried to get my drawings. He said I came to the Metro Centre, then he was told he can't access his drawings and as he was leaving an official approached him and said listen - I can get hold of your drawing for you.

(Masa) The official was - in effect - allegedly offering to do his job in exchange for a bribe. After some negotiation one thousand five hundred Rand was transferred to him.

(Daniel Schay) So you get the drawings you go make your own copies and you return (them). So that puts the integrity of the entire archives into question.

(Masa) And it wasn’t an isolated incident.

(Daniel Schay) Next time, another councillor approached me, he said a resident of mine says the department is charging nine hundred to one thousand four hundred Rand for drawings. I said that's not official department policy.

(Masa) But who exactly was the official in question? Schay gave us a phone number and a name: Norman. The details looked familiar, and no wonder… Norman Munyai was our helpful insider!

(Masa) When we met Norman earlier this year, we took care to hide his identity, believing he was an honest civil servant trying to improve the city’s services. That’s why you’ll only see his legs in our undercover footage.
(Producer) (Subtitles) Do you know how many files are here?
(Norman) (Subtitles) I can't tell exactly. Just because here is an archive for the whole City of Johannesburg
(Masa) You can imagine our shock when we realised Norman was the man allegedly soliciting bribes from desperate residents.

(Masa) Our attempt to catch Norman redhanded failed when this article appeared in the Sunday Times and he went to ground.

(Masa) Instead, we gave him a call.

(Masa) So you didn't solicit any bribes?

(Norman) No, I didn't take any bribes

(Masa) So I'll ask you clearly, did you take any money from any resident in the City of Joburg for building plans?

(Norman) No.

(Masa) Ironically, Norman insists the allegation must be untrue because the building is closed. The very building he let us into.

(Norman) Where we are there's no plans and the building was closed.

(Masa) You gave them those building plans so they can go and make photocopies. You accepted that money, that is called a bribe Norman.

(Norman)(Subtitles) Give me the evidence that you gave me cash.

(Masa) You're running a slick operation. I like your hovering on the evidence part because you know how you're going about this operation to ensure that obviously, that there is no paper trail.

(Norman) (Subtitles) For me - I'm telling you - if there's someone who has evidence come to me.

(Masa) According to Schay, Norman’s superiors are doing the same: demanding evidence rather than acting on complaints.

(Daniel Schay) If the administration and the political leadership is unwilling to open up proper investigations into officials, we will never deal with corruption.

(Masa) We got in touch with Norman’s employer: the City of Johannesburg - it says, there's currently no evidence against Norman but that an investigation has been launched into the complaints."

(Masa) Unfortunately, this is further proof of the domino effect of poor service delivery: an opportunity to make a quick buck from you, the taxpayer.
